stories.summary: Nigeria: The Deepwater Tax Incentive Debate - Will the Billions Reach Nigerians? 17 August 2026 Daily Trust (Abuja) By Halimah Nuhu Sanda There is a point at which economic policy stops being a subject for economists and oil executives and becomes everyone's business. Nigeria may have reached that point again with the federal government's new rules-based fiscal framework for deep offshore oil and gas projects, which it says could unlock up to $50 billion in investment. The ambition is significant because Nigeria has a peculiar contradiction: enormous petroleum resources beneath its waters, but billions of dollars of capital sitting on the sidelines because some projects have not been commercially attractive enough to proceed. The government is betting that a more predictable and competitive fiscal regime can change that calculation. It is easy, particularly in the current economic climate, to dislike the idea of giving oil companies tax incentives.

Fourteen years after the Marikana Massacre, survivors, victims' families and trade unions are still calling for accountability. The massacre resulted in a total of 40 deaths and 78 injuries, with mineworkers accounting for the vast majority of casualties. On 16 August 2012, 34 miners participating in a wildcat strike at the Lonmin platinum mine at Marikana, near Rustenberg, to demand pay of R12,500 a month up from R4,000 a month, were gunned down by the South African Police Services (SAPS) at two separate killing sites. stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The captives were held in Ghana's Cape Coast Castle before being forced into ships to take them across the Atlantic Ocean By Aleem Maqbool Religion editor ,Â Reporting from Accra, Ghana Published 7 hours ago This year has seen a dramatic change in tone in the global conversation about the transatlantic slave trade. The demand for formal apologies, debt relief and financial compensation from nations and institutions that benefited from slavery has become increasingly forceful. In March, a resolution was passed at the United Nations recognising slavery as "the greatest crime against humanity" - though the United States voted against the resolution and every European nation abstained from the vote. The UK, which alongside Portugal dominated the transatlantic slave trade, has consistently rejected the idea of paying reparations, which is perhaps unsurprising given estimates of what Britain "owes" in damages to nations affected run into many trillions of pounds . This resistance has not deterred the country that has become the leading voice on reparations: Ghana.

stories.title: Zimbabwe boat accident death toll hits 68 as 22 more bodies recovered
stories.summary: A coffin with the body of a victim of the capsized passenger ferry, leaves the Kariba hospital mortuary after his body was identified for burial in Kariba, on 14 August 2026. Photograph: Jekesai Njikizana/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A coffin with the body of a victim of the capsized passenger ferry, leaves the Kariba hospital mortuary after his body was identified for burial in Kariba, on 14 August 2026. Photograph: Jekesai Njikizana/AFP/Getty Images Zimbabwe boat accident death toll hits 68 as 22 more bodies recovered Eighteen children among the people killed after ferry capsized on Lake Kariba Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe , taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday. The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba , on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

stories.title: Zimbabwe : le bilan monte à 84 morts dans le naufrage d'un ferry sur le lac Kariba
stories.summary: Publicité Zimbabwe : le bilan monte à 84 morts dans le naufrage d'un ferry sur le lac Kariba Afrique Un ferry de passagers surchargé a chaviré mardi sur le lac Kariba, au Zimbabwe. Le bilan a été revu à la hausse dimanche après la découverte de nouveaux corps, portant à 84 le nombre de personnes noyées, selon la police. Publié le : 16/08/2026 - 16:36 Modifié le : 16/08/2026 - 22:02 3 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Les secouristes et les exploitants de bateaux locaux participent aux opérations de recherche et de sauvetage en cours sur le lac Kariba, au lendemain du chavirement d'un bateau, à Kariba, au Zimbabwe, le 12 août 2026. © Admore Mbonda, Reuters Un bilan qui ne cesse d'augmenter. stories.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 17, 2026
stories.summary: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 17, 2026 AllAfrica AllAfrica logo 17 August 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda Morocco Detains Over 100 Migrants Near Ceuta Border Moroccan authorities have detained more than 100 migrants near the border with Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta amid fears of another mass crossing. At least 111 people, mostly from sub-Saharan Africa, were reportedly detained around Fnideq. Police used tear gas to disperse groups gathered near the border. It comes a fortnight after roughly 78,000 migrants arrived in the exclave by sea in a matter of hours - 100 of whom died, according to the city's mayor, who also said the vast majority of arrivals had returned to Morocco. Morocco and Spain have deployed thousands of security personnel, drones, boats and barriers.

stories.title: Les anciens d’Azrou au sommet de l’État marocain
stories.summary: À la fin du Protectorat, en 1956, le royaume reprend en main l’appareil d’un État devenu indépendant, au sein duquel les anciens élèves d’Azrou vont occuper une place importante, dans toutes les sphères du pouvoir. Des rangs de l’armée aux coulisses du palais en passant par les bureaux de l’administration, ils sont incontournables.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: les journalistes désormais contraints de suivre une formation militaire
stories.summary: Burkina Faso: les journalistes désormais contraints de suivre une formation militaire Plus de 40 journalistes burkinabè viennent de participer à une formation militaire au « patriotisme » pendant plusieurs jours, près de Ouagadougou. Présentée comme une nouvelle obligation dans le contexte de guerre contre les groupes djihadistes dans lequel vit le pays, l'initiative suscite une vive inquiétude chez tous les défenseurs de la liberté de la presse, à commencer par Reporters sans frontières (RSF). Publié le : 15/08/2026 - 17:31 Modifié le : 16/08/2026 - 02:14 2 min Temps de lecture «Un journaliste professionnel et pas patriote est une menace», a notamment déclaré le ministre burkinabè de la Communication lors d'une visite à l'Académie militaire de Pabré où s'est déroulée la formation. © rfi Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Plus de 40 journalistes burkinabè de médias publics et privés viennent de suivre une formation militaire présentée par la junte au pouvoir comme une « immersion patriotique » qui aura désormais lieu chaque année. Si, dans le contexte de guerre contre les groupes djihadistes dans lequel vit le pays, une initiative du même genre avait déjà été rendue obligatoire l'an dernier pour les élèves admis au baccalauréat, cette nouvelle disposition inquiète les défenseurs de la liberté de la presse, d'autant plus des journalistes burkinabè ont déjà été réquisitionnés de force pour combattre et que la presse nationale subit une forte pression du pouvoir, comme vient le rappeler le cas de Serge Oulon, qui est toujours détenu deux ans après son enlèvement à Ouagadougou. Pour Yao Noël, président de L’Union des journalistes de la presse libre africaine (UJPLA), la place des journalistes n'est pas dans les camps militaires.

stories.title: Senegal hikes fuel prices amid surge in global oil markets
stories.summary: Senegal has raised fuel prices in a move the government says is necessary because of the sharp rise in global oil costs.

stories.title: Tributes pour in for Jason Arday after his sudden death
stories.summary: Friends have paid tribute to British sociologist and professor Jason Arday following his death, days after he stepped down from Cambridge amid intense scrutiny over plagiarism allegations.

stories.title: Ceuta: pas d'arrivée massive aux abords de l'enclave, un important dispositif sécuritaire déployé
stories.summary: Ceuta: pas d'arrivée massive aux abords de l'enclave, un important dispositif sécuritaire déployé Alors que des appels à un nouveau franchissement, ce week-end, des frontières entre le Maroc et les enclaves espagnoles de Ceuta et de Melilla ont circulé sur les réseaux sociaux, ces derniers ne semblent pas avoir, cette fois, trouvé d'écho. Si les commanditaires de ces messages partagés des dizaines de milliers de fois en ligne n'ont toujours pas été clairement identifiés, le Maroc a mis en place un énorme dispositif de sécurité pour éviter toute migration clandestine. Publié le : 15/08/2026 - 16:02 Modifié le : 15/08/2026 - 16:10 2 min Temps de lecture L'Espagne et le Maroc ont considérablement renforcé leurs dispositifs de sécurité respectifs aux frontières des enclaves de Ceuta et de Melilla pour dissuader toute nouvelle tentative de franchissement après de nouveaux appels en ce sens pour le week-end du 15 août. © AP Photo/Antonio Sempere Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre envoyé spécial à Fnideq, François Hume-Ferkatadji Aucun mouvement d’arrivée massif n'a pour l'instant été détecté dans la ville marocaine de Fnideq frontalière de l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta, ce samedi 15 août. Quadrillée par les forces de l’ordre , la cité est, depuis vendredi 14 août, le théâtre de nombreux contrôles par des agents en civil qui appréhendent les jeunes jugés suspects pour les soumettre à des interrogatoires ou des procédures d’éloignement. Alors que des zodiacs de la police patrouillent également en mer, le Maroc a en outre annoncé avoir construit une nouvelle ligne de barbelés proche du poste-frontière.

stories.title: Burkina Faso imposes military training on journalists
stories.summary: More than 40 journalists in Burkina Faso have taken part in a military-style "patriotism" training course imposed by the authoritarian ruling junta.

stories.title: « Le pétrole est une malédiction » : en Ouganda, des villages dans l’incertitude sur la propriété de leurs terres
stories.summary: En Ouganda, la ruée vers l’or noir a exacerbé des conflits fonciers vieux de quinze ans. TotalEnergies et Kampala s’y retrouvent face aux communautés spoliées. Reportage.

stories.title: UN says $50 million ransom fueled Al-Qaeda offensive in Mali
stories.summary: According to a new UN report, most of the money was redistributed to fighters in the Sahel, while some was passed on to Al-Qaeda’s affiliate in the Arabian Peninsula and to the group’s central command.

stories.title: Succès Masra gracié, Assimi Goïta et Abdelmadjid Tebboune se réconcilient, la crise d’Ormuz profite aux majors… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer
stories.summary: Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique revient sur la grâce accordée à l’opposant tchadien Succès Masra, décrypte la réconciliation entre le Mali et l’Algérie, analyse les bénéfices tirés par les majors de la crise d’Ormuz et le regain d’attractivité des hydrocarbures africains, s’interroge sur un possible report des élections locales au Sénégal et fait le point sur les dernières tractations autour du dialogue national en RDC.

stories.title: Morocco and Spain boost security in Ceuta as another call for border rush seen online
stories.summary: Moroccan authorities on Wednesday announced measures to counter a new influx of migrants to the Spanish territory of Ceuta, after monitoring a new wave of online disinformation.

stories.summary: Otage américain au Niger : comment l’administration Trump a obtenu la libération Enlevé à Niamey en octobre 2024, le missionnaire américain Kevin Rideout a été libéré aprés dix mois de captivité. stories.title: Au Kenya, la mort préoccupante d’éléphants, victimes de mystérieux empoisonnements
stories.summary: Au moins 16 pachydermes sont morts dans des circonstances inexpliquées depuis le mois de juin dans la région d’Amboseli, dans le sud du Kenya. L’hypothèse d’une intoxication due à des pesticides est remise en cause par plusieurs experts.

stories.title: UN calls for negotiations to end the conflict in Mozambique
stories.summary: A military victory over jihadist insurgents in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province does not appear imminent, according to a report by a United Nations special rapporteur released Friday.

stories.title: The Polygamist's author says women see themselves reflected in her Netflix hit
stories.summary: Image caption, Sue Nyathi says people call her an overnight success but "the work has been put in over many years" By Megha Mohan BBC World Service Published 15 August 2026 When Sue Nyathi sent her debut novel The Polygamist to publishers, "they thought there was no market for the book" about a married Zimbabwean man and the women he seduces, she says. So the Zimbabwean author found her own editor, typesetter and artist, and in 2012 published 500 copies herself. It defied the publishers' predictions and became a huge hit. It has now been adapted for Netflix and is in the top 10 of the platform's most streamed series in more than 60 countries, reaching number two in the United States. Hollywood actress Taraji P Henson said the series had her in a "chokehold" and she binge-watched all 22 episodes in a single day.

stories.title: Au Soudan, une attaque des paramilitaires des FSR fait au moins 14 morts parmi les civils au Kordofan du Nord
stories.summary: Des dizaines d’autres personnes ont été blessées lors de cet assaut mené par les rebelles à Umm Arda, à environ 200 kilomètres au sud de la capitale, Khartoum. Plusieurs villes soudanaises sont le théâtre d’attaques de plus en plus intenses menées par les FSR.

stories.title: Central African Republic: Muslims return as Sibut rebuilds
stories.summary: Years after civil war drove many Muslims from Sibut, the call to prayer is echoing again from the town’s rebuilt central mosque. Returning residents and Christian neighbours are seeking to restore trust and revive a community once known for peaceful coexistence.

stories.title: Côte d’Ivoire : qui est Martial Yavo, le nouveau général de Charles Blé Goudé ?
stories.summary: Côte d’Ivoire : qui est Martial Yavo, le nouveau général de Charles Blé Goudé ? stories.title: Guinée : Bella Bah, un « activiste dans l’âme » qui dérange Mamadi Doumbouya
stories.summary: Guinée : Bella Bah, un « activiste dans l’âme » qui dérange Mamadi Doumbouya L’ancien membre du Front national de défense de la Constitution (FNDC) a été enlevé dans l’école dont il est le directeur, samedi 8 août. stories.title: Comment l’Afrique du Sud a doublé l’Espagne sur l’exportation d’agrumes
stories.summary: En quarante ans, l’Afrique du Sud est passée des boycotts anti-apartheid au sommet du commerce mondial des agrumes. Mais protectionnisme européen, logistique défaillante et El Niño menacent ce succès.

stories.title: La Cour africaine des droits de l’homme est-elle encore utile ?
stories.summary: Créée pour protéger les droits fondamentaux sur le continent, la Cour africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples (CADHP) peine à faire appliquer ses décisions : sur les 104 arrêts rendus, seuls deux ont été pleinement exécutés.

stories.title: South African lawmakers question effectiveness of army deployment against gang Violence
stories.summary: Officials have maintained that the military deployment is intended to support—not replace—long-term policing efforts, but lawmakers say urgent changes are needed if the operation is to have any meaningful impact.

stories.title: Zambia Halts Presidential Election Vote Count Over Violence and Fraud Allegations
stories.summary: The electoral commission for the southern African nation said poll workers had been attacked and ballots had been stolen.

stories.title: RDC : la loi sur le référendum renvoyée devant le Parlement, Félix Tshisekedi maître des horloges
stories.summary: Le président, Félix Tshisekedi, a renvoyé au Parlement la loi référendaire en demandant la modification de certains de ses articles. Un report qui intervient au moment où l’opposition appelle à l’apaisement avant l’ouverture d’un potentiel dialogue national.

stories.title: Quand les élèves d’Azrou se retournent contre le Protectorat
stories.summary: La « politique berbère » du Protectorat reposait sur le maintien des élèves du collège d’Azrou à distance des courants qui agitaient le reste du Maroc. Pourtant, au début des années 1940, les certitudes de « la Résidence » se lézardent. Au cœur même de son dispositif scolaire émerge une conscience politique qu’elle n’a su ni anticiper ni contenir.

stories.title: Au Soudan du Sud, plus de 650 000 réfugiés menacés de perdre l’aide de l’ONU
stories.summary: Cette situation « survient au pire moment possible. Avec la saison des pluies qui atteint son pic, l’accès devient plus difficile, les prix de la nourriture augmentent et les familles disposent d’encore moins de solutions pour faire face à la situation », a alerté le représentant adjoint du HCR au Soudan du Sud.

stories.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Counting began on Thursday evening as soon as polls had closed By Dingindaba Buyoya BBC Focus on Africa Published 13 August 2026 Updated 14 August 2026 Zambia's electoral commission has resumed the counting of votes from Thursday's presidential, parliamentary and local elections after it was halted over alleged attacks on polling staff. The authority paused the process nationwide expressing concern about reports of violence that had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes". President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second five-year term. Brian Mundubile is the main opposition candidate among 13 challengers. The electoral commission has set itself the target of announcing the results by the end of Sunday.

stories.title: China and Egypt launch second joint air force exercise
stories.summary: The exercises reflect growing defense ties between Beijing and Cairo as both countries expand military cooperation through joint training and strategic exchanges.

stories.title: « On est en train de perdre notre jeunesse » : dans le nord du Maroc, l’ombre des noyés de Ceuta
stories.summary: A Tétouan, les familles se désespèrent après la mort de nombreux hommes qui ont tenté le passage à la nage jusqu’à l’enclave espagnole, fin juillet. Au total, plus de 140 d’entre eux auraient perdu la vie, selon une ONG marocaine. Malgré ces drames, beaucoup rêvent encore de gagner clandestinement l’Europe.

stories.title: Zambia's opposition leader expresses 'grave concern' as vote count suspended
stories.summary: Just hours after Zambia’s electoral commission suspended vote counting nationwide, opposition presidential candidate Brian Mundubile raised “grave concern,” calling for full transparency amid reports of violence.

stories.title: Croatia wildfire near Omiš injures residents and disrupts holiday travel
stories.summary: A major wildfire near Omiš, around 25 kilometres south-east of Split, forced about 1,200 residents and tourists to evacuate overnight on Thursday and into Friday as strong winds drove the flames towards the coastal town.

stories.title: Zambia resumes counting after violence disrupts election process
stories.summary: Zambia has resumed vote counting after a nationwide suspension over election-related violence, with the Electoral Commission saying security threats have been contained. The first presidential results are expected at 10:00 p.m. local time, or 2000 GMT.

stories.title: Worries grow over mysterious illness killing Kenyan elephants
stories.summary: Worries over the death of elephants are mounting in southern Kenya, where at least 19 animals have died since June from an unexplained condition. With symptoms including partial paralysis, conservationists and communities are demanding urgent investigations into what is killing the elephants.

stories.title: Au Sénégal, le patrimoine de Bassirou Diomaye Faye au cœur d’un nouveau bras de fer avec Ousmane Sonko
stories.summary: Le Pastef veut contraindre Bassirou Diomaye Faye à déclarer son patrimoine en fin de mandat. Le chef de l’État contre-attaque en visant aussi Ousmane Sonko. Analyse d’un nouvel épisode de la guerre à laquelle se livrent les deux hommes.

stories.title: Barrick : pourquoi l’Afrique reste au cœur de la stratégie internationale du géant minier
stories.summary: En séparant ses actifs nord-américains du reste, Barrick redessine son portefeuille mondial. À la tête du « Rest of the world », Sebastiaan Bock hérite d’un ensemble où l’Afrique pourrait peser lourd.

stories.title: Congo's Ebola cases rising at record pace
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5Io4L Fear of Ebola infections is growing in Congo, as there is still no vaccine available against the current virulent strain of the disease Image: Xin Huashefa/Xinhua/picture alliance Advertisement The Ebola epidemic in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province in the country. Concerns are growing that the life-threatening infectious disease could reach the capital, Kinshasa, which is home to 19 million people. Facilities for isolating patients are ready for the event that a public health alert should hit the capital, said Jean-Jacques Muyembe, head of Congo's National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). "If there is a suspected case, the epidemiological services and the INRB laboratory are ready to quickly identify and confirm cases," he told DW. "The Ministry of Health has set up the Cinquantenaire Hospital so that it can admit and fully isolate patients if necessary. We can quickly contain an Ebola outbreak here in Kinshasa." The peak of the Ebola outbreak is expected to arrive in about six months Image: Badru Katumba/AFP Health crisis still in the making However, the virus has been spreading faster than health authorities can contain it. This Ebola outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which no vaccine or treatment has yet been approved.

stories.title: Mustafa Rawji (Rawbank) : « Notre priorité, c’est désormais l’économie réelle, celle qui crée de l’emploi »
stories.summary: Face aux défis de la RDC et à l’émergence de la concurrence, Rawbank adapte son modèle. Son dirigeant veut conforter la position de leader régional de la banque, en axant sur les PME et les investisseurs internationaux attirés par les grands projets régionaux.

stories.title: Le dépouillement de l'élection présidentielle interrompu en Zambie du fait de violences
stories.summary: Publicité Le dépouillement de l'élection présidentielle interrompu en Zambie du fait de violences Afrique La commission électorale zambienne a annoncé jeudi la suspension du dépouillement de l'élection présidentielle, invoquant des violences. Edgar Lungu Brian Mundubile, figure de proue de l'opposition, affirme avoir remporté le scrutin, dont l'issue devrait être connue le 17 août. Publié le : 14/08/2026 - 14:46 Modifié le : 14/08/2026 - 14:54 3 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Une femme dépose son bulletin de vote dans un bureau de vote à Lusaka, capitale de la Zambie, le 13 août 2026. © Gianluigi Guercia, AFP Le dépouillement des élections présidentielle et parlementaires, organisées jeudi 14 août en Zambie , est suspendu pour au moins 24 heures en raison de "violences", a annoncé vendredi la commission électorale de ce pays d' Afrique australe. Le principal opposant, Brian Mundubile, a un peu plus tôt revendiqué la victoire dès le premier tour, tandis que le président sortant Hakainde Hichilema a réagi en appelant les Zambiens à rester "patients". "La commission électorale de Zambie a pris connaissance avec inquiétude des informations faisant état de violences survenues lors du dépouillement et de la proclamation des résultats dans certains districts. (...) Compte tenu de la situation sécuritaire et des menaces persistantes de violence, la commission a suspendu, avec effet immédiat, le dépouillement et la proclamation des résultats", a déclaré devant les médias à Lusaka le directeur des élections à la commission, Brown Kasaro. "La commission réexaminera cette suspension dans les 24 heures", a-t-il ajouté. La victoire revendiquée par une coalition de partis d'opposition À la tête d'une coalition de partis d'opposition et rival le plus sérieux de "HH, l'ancien ministre de l'ex-président Edgar Lungu Brian Mundubile a affirmé dans une vidéo diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux avoir "remporté cette élection tant au niveau présidentiel qu'en termes de majorité des sièges au Parlement" juste avant cette annonce.

stories.title: Elections présidentielle et parlementaires en Zambie : le dépouillement suspendu en raison de « violences », annonce la Commission électorale
stories.summary: Peu avant l’annonce, Brian Mundubile, principal opposant au président sortant Hakainde Hichilema, a revendiqué la victoire dès le premier tour, tandis que M. Hichilema a réagi en appelant les Zambiens à rester « patients ».

stories.title: Dîna Slaoui, la Marocaine qui a ouvert les portes du monde très fermé des diamantaires
stories.summary: Première Marocaine à intégrer la Bourse du diamant d’Anvers, Dîna Slaoui s’est frayé un chemin dans un univers où réputation et confiance font loi. De Casablanca aux coulisses du négoce mondial, portrait d’une passionnée qui connaît les diamants sous toutes leurs facettes.

stories.title: Niger-Algérie : Sonatrach marque un point dans la réalisation de ses ambitions pétrolières
stories.summary: La compagnie pétrolière algérienne Sonatrach vient de lancer les opérations de forage d’un puit à Kafra, dans le nord du Niger. Une façon pour les deux pays d’acter leur rapprochement après des mois de tensions diplomatiques.

stories.title: Qui est Emaar, le groupe émirati qui signe son retour au Maroc ?
stories.summary: Qui est Emaar, le groupe émirati qui signe son retour au Maroc ? Spécialiste des mégaprojets immobiliers, Emaar, fondé par Mohamed Alabbar, pourrait construire un nouveau complexe dans la région de Casablanca. stories.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months

Kevin Rideout was kidnapped in Niger’s capital and no armed group claimed responsibility for the abduction. Where did we get lost?’ Zimbabwe reckons with the reality of violence against women The deaths of a Bulawayo mother and her daughters spark calls for an urgent action on gender-based violence T he three white coffins were draped in white lace and topped with small sprays of flowers. stories.title: Presidential pardon for French alleged spy accused of plotting Mali coup
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, President Assimi GoÃ¯ta (pictured) has pardoned French national Yann Vezilier By Natasha Booty Â and Â Wycliffe Muia Published 13 August 2026 A Frenchman who was sentenced to 20 years in prison in Mali for plotting an alleged coup in the West African country has now been granted a presidential pardon, it was announced on Thursday. Yann Vezilier was accused a year ago of trying to destabilise President Assimi GoÃ¯ta's government "on behalf of the French intelligence service" alongside a number of army generals and dozens of soldiers. It is not yet clear what has prompted Mali's U-turn. France's foreign ministry has yet to comment on the pardoning, and previously said accusations that Vezilier was working in Mali as a French spy were "unfounded". In a post on Facebook , external , the Malian government said: "This act of clemency, which does not call into question the facts established by an adversarial judgment rendered during a trial, where all rights of the defence were respected, is accompanied by the immediate removal of the individual from national territory." Mali is a former colony of France, and has been gripped by a security crisis fuelled by an Islamist insurgency since 2012.

stories.title: DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province

Photograph: Dieudonne Dirole/AP DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago. The current outbreak has killed more than 2,100 people out of more than 4,500 cases, according to the latest government figures released on Tuesday. At the same point in the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa , the previous most deadly outbreak, 755 cases had been recorded, according to WHO data.

stories.title: Eritrea, a rising power along a global shipping artery
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5Igaq Eritrea's location at the Bab Al-Mandab Strait is an asset for the autocratic nation, as partners from near and far seek access to the Red Sea Image: ABACA/picture alliance Advertisement Across the Horn of Africa , geopolitical interests of various countries continue to cause tensions and conflict as part of the growing competition for political influence over the region. In its own right, the small country of Eritrea appears to be gaining in importance within this context. The autocratic state run by long-standing ruler Isaias Afwerki controls strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea, especially with its ports of Assab and Massawa. In July, a series of diplomatic consultations in Cairo involving regional powers like Egypt, Somalia , Eritrea, and a high-ranking US envoy highlighted Eritrea's growing role in helping to coordinate approaches to resolving serious security challenges in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, and to facilitate trade. Eritrea's unique location along this maritime route is notably becoming more and more strategic in light of international trade conflicts.

stories.title: Ayra Starr on her secret relationship and teasing Stevie Wonder
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Ayra Starr is a multiple Grammy and Mobo Award nominee, for hit songs like Rush, Commas, Sability and Gimme Dat By Mark Savage Music correspondent Published 13 August 2026 There's resilience, and then there's Ayra Starr. Two weeks before the release of her new album, Starrgirl, the Nigerian singer posted a photo from hospital, after undergoing "major surgery". "I was hoping it would be a quick recovery, but it was more complicated than they expected," she told fans , external , without disclosing the nature of the procedure. Within seven days, she was back in the dance studio, rehearsing for forthcoming performances with a large bandage strapped across her stomach. TV appearances, fan events and live performances followed. "I'm healing," she told the US breakfast TV show, Today. "I have strength today. I'm so happy I was able to even be here today and be able to do this." It's a display of the tenacity and ambition that's defined Starr's career to date.

stories.title: Vultures are disappearing in Nigeria - but the 'Vulture King' is fighting to reverse the trend
stories.summary: Image source, Universal Images Group via Getty Images Image caption, Some see them as sinister but these birds play a vital role in nature's cycle By Makuochi Okafor BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Awka-Etiti, Nigeria Published 13 August 2026 "People fear the environment where the shrine is. So, nobody fights vultures that perch here," a man they call the Vulture King tells the BBC. Mostly associated with death and decay, perhaps it is not surprising that when vultures disappeared from the skies across many West African cities, they were not missed. Yet across the continent, their disappearance is becoming impossible to ignore, as conservationists warn that hunting linked to traditional beliefs and spiritual practices continues to threaten several vulture species to the point of near extinction. Without vultures, ecosystems would lose a natural defence against the spread of disease.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Kariba Boat Disaster - Rising Death Toll Exposes Rida 'Lies', Passenger Figures Under Scrutiny As Body Count Hits 84
stories.summary: Zimbabwe: Kariba Boat Disaster - Rising Death Toll Exposes Rida 'Lies', Passenger Figures Under Scrutiny As Body Count Hits 84 17 August 2026 New Zimbabwe (London) THE number of people aboard the ill-fated Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA) boat on Lake Kariba appears to have been higher than the 153 passengers previously indicated, with the latest death toll and rescue figures accounting for at least 161 people. The Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) said Sunday that four more bodies had been recovered from the lake, pushing the death toll to 84. "The ZRP reports that the death toll is now 84 after the recovery of four bodies from the lake this afternoon," police said in its latest update. The latest figures raise fresh questions over the number of people who were actually aboard the RIDA vessel when it capsized. stories.title: Ceuta showed just how easily Europe can be divided
stories.summary: Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters View image in fullscreen Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters Ceuta showed just how easy it is to divide Europe Paul Taylor The migrant influx prompted recriminations and a tit-for-tat dispute between Italy and Spain. Putin, Erdoğan and others will have taken note W ithin hours of the first pictures of tens of thousands of migrants swimming the short distance from Morocco to the Spanish north African enclave of Ceuta hitting social media on 30 July, 22 European Union leaders , the Trump administration and Israel had piled on to criticise Madrid. The outbreak of hysteria and recrimination was a case study in 21st-century politics, driven by real-time images in a media echo chamber where populists set the agenda on migration, propagating fear, prejudice and demagogic proposals.

stories.title: A burial row over Zambia's late president has turned its election into a hot contest
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, More than eight million registered voters have 14 presidential candidates to choose from By Dingindaba Buyoya BBC Focus on Africa ,Â Reporting from Lusaka Published 11 August 2026 A spectre is hanging over the Zambian election campaign in the shape of former President Edgar Lungu. Despite having died more than a year ago in South Africa, his body remains unburied amid a bitter dispute between President Hakainde Hichilema and the Lungu family that has sharpened political divisions. This has had a role in energising support for the opposition National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), particularly in the northern half of the country, traditional strongholds of Lungu's Patriotic Front (PF), as people see it as offering the best chance to unseat the incumbent. Meanwhile, it has complicated the second-term bid of Hichilema and his United Party for National Development (UPND), which draws its core support from the south, west and north-west while seeking to expand its reach nationwide. The political battle is playing out on the streets of the capital, Lusaka.

stories.title: Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho
stories.summary: Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films View image in fullscreen Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films Review Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese pairs his literary-grade voiceover with propulsive, prophetic images to interrogate his identity and that of his colonialism-carved homeland H ere is a captivating stream of consciousness film about exile, roots and identity by Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese, director of the lauded 2019 activism story This Is Not a Burial, It’s a Resurrection . It’s ostensibly a cine-memoir looking back from the vantage point of present-day Berlin to his upbringing in Lesotho, narrated by Mosese’s dense, literary-grade voiceover. But there’s something propulsive and prophetic about the accompanying hyper-vivid images from rural and urban life.
